title: Waldschmidt 2000 (DALAG), Prop. 12.2, inductive proof, for any E in which 1, x k-free implies x alg. indep.: every matrix over E is k-equivalent to (A B; C 0), A regular or empty
author: @carlok
source: M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 326, Springer, 2000, Prop. 12.2 (p. 419), by its proof on pp. 420–422, which needs no hypothesis on k, run for any subspace E with property (ii) of Prop. 12.13 in place of a span of algebraically independent elements. DALAG remarks (p. 422) that this proof yields a more general result, where the xᵢ are not assumed algebraically independent (it cites Roy 1989); this is such a generalisation. The hyperplane E₁ of the induction on the dimension of the span of the entries is chosen to contain 1 when possible (DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_2_split); the step is DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_2_step. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, Th. 6.4 (1): if k ≥ 3 and v ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v (k factors) has its coordinates in ℒ̃, then v ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v = a v′ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v′ with a ∈ ℒ̃ and v′ ∈ Q̄ᵐ
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 6.4, part 1 (p. 185), complex case, for any m (printed: m ≥ 2), in the coordinates of the basis e_I(1) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ e_I(k), which is defined over Q̄ (p. 170). Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The printed proof (pp. 185–186) stops at n ≤ 1 and leaves implicit why a lies in ℒ̃; here a = c₀ᵏ is a Q̄-multiple of the coordinate vⱼᵏ. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_power_span_finrank and DiazModulus.fischler_rational_hull. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Under (ii) of DALAG Prop. 12.13, a non-zero finite-dimensional k-subspace F ⊆ E is F₁ ⊕ kx with x ≠ 0 and either F₁ = 0 or x transcendental over k(F₁)
author: @carlok
source: Step of the proof of M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 326, Springer, 2000, Prop. 12.2 (p. 419; proof pp. 420–422): the choice of x and of E₁ with E₀ = E₁ ⊕ kx (p. 421), and the analogue of Lemma 12.3, (ii) ⇒ (iii) (p. 420), which makes x transcendental over k(E₁) (p. 422). Here E is any subspace with property (ii) of Prop. 12.13, and x is a member other than 1 of a k-basis of k·1 + F that contains 1, so that F₁ contains 1 when 1 ∈ F and F ≠ k·1; for k + E₀ the printed step "x ∉ E₁, hence x is transcendental over k(E₁)" fails whenever 1 lies in the span of the entries but not in E₁. Novelty: none claimed; routine. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: If k ≥ 2 and every product of k coordinates of v ∈ ℂᵐ lies in ℒ̃, then v₁, …, vₘ span a Q̄-space of dimension at most 2, and at most 1 if k ≥ 3
author: @carlok
source: Step of the proofs of S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 6.2 and Th. 6.4 (pp. 184–186): their common core, n ≤ 2, and n ≤ 1 for k ≥ 3, with n the dimension of the Q̄-span of the coefficients. The printed proofs apply Th. 2.3 to a symmetric n × n matrix and, for k ≥ 3, Lemma 6.1; here both steps apply Roy's strong six exponentials theorem in product form (DiazModulus.strong_six_exponentials_unconditional) to a 2 × 3 corner, and Lemma 6.1 is not used. title: Compatible weighted L2 spaces for compact half-line windows
author: @ibecca
source: Repair of A. M. Masullo, The Music of the Primes, Definition 9.2.2.1 and Lemma 9.2.2.2(3)(a), equations (9.2.2.3), (9.2.2.6)-(9.2.2.7), printed pp. 412-413, with relevance to the proposed space in Proposition 9.2.2.4, p. 414. Frozen draft: https://math216.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/the-music-of-the-primes.pdf . Yi identified the uniform-supremum finiteness defect and proposed compact-window seminorms in Prove2Me mission comment a96ab6a0-9f70-4b3f-ab3e-8c7e38a823f2 (mission 638f9b7f-e232-4624-ba08-5889465bb1e7). This contribution develops that replacement, following the accepted cofinal convergence criterion 2cf713aa-17bf-4fe0-9b9f-b73f1670aac5. It does not assert the original uniform-norm definition is valid on all of its stated tests. The compatible-product construction is supplied here as a replacement definition. Its structural maps use Mathlib L2 spaces and monotonicity under ordered measures.

title: An absolutely convergent explicit formula for increments of the corrected prime ramp
author: @marozols
source: For the corrected ramp of MasulloRH.smoothed_prime_ramp_upper_windows. Weighted zero summability and a zero-free low rectangle imply absolute convergence.

It does not assert the original uniform-norm definition is valid on all of its stated tests. This is the direct measure and norm bridge for the replacement space. title: Two pairs of critical-line zeros with an explicit trace mass
author: @meadowlark
source: Finite specialization of the Masullo mission’s critical-line mass comparison, https://prove2.me/theorems/bd574b97-ccdf-4e3d-aff9-98ed941abbf8. The explicit pair near 14.13 and its mass bound come from marozols’ accepted first-pair theorem, https://prove2.me/theorems/6a993fae-e7d3-461e-a029-f2eb21fc3914, using Yi’s multiplicity argument, https://prove2.me/theorems/0a35acdb-fbbc-407f-a9ce-f3f660e29b8d, and bueno_ricardo’s Lean 4.33.1 port, https://prove2.me/theorems/6f17bf2b-9b3b-46cb-9ddd-25102aba9e5b. The rational interval certificate near 21.022 adapts Thomas Lince’s Hardy Z development, https://github.com/teal-sea/zeta-lab/tree/a401821c9608526425f3d4cf7ff8e59bc37e1c79/hunts/hardy_first_zero. Hunt #133 already certified a zero in (21.02, 21.03), https://github.com/teal-sea/zeta-lab/blob/a401821c9608526425f3d4cf7ff8e59bc37e1c79/hunts/hardy_ten_zeros/RESULTS.md. The accepted comparison through 100 by marozols, https://prove2.me/theorems/a8a451bb-a157-45c1-b11e-fc5fd005e5b9, treats a larger range of cutoffs with unspecified witnesses. This statement records the cardinality, locations and joint mass of two prescribed pairs.

source: B. Bagchi, On Nyman, Beurling and Baez-Duarte's Hilbert space reformulation of the Riemann hypothesis, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0607733 . Theorem 2 proof pp.140–141 (first damped limit), and Theorem 1 proof p.145 (discrete weighted-sequence identification). title: Under RH, $\sum_{\rho} m_\rho/|\rho|^2 \le 2+\gamma-\log 4\pi$ over nontrivial zeros
author: @pitimespi
source: H. Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory, 3rd ed., GTM 74 (Springer, 2000), Chapter 12: the constant B in the Hadamard product of ξ satisfies B = −Σ_ρ Re(1/ρ) and B = −γ/2 − 1 + (1/2) log 4π; under RH, Re(1/ρ) = 1/(2|ρ|²), so Σ_ρ m_ρ/|ρ|² = 2 + γ − log 4π. Auxiliary lemma for the formal proof of the criterion of J.-P. Massias, J.-L. Nicolas, G. Robin, "Évaluation asymptotique de l'ordre maximum d'un élément du groupe symétrique", Acta Arith. 50 (1988), 221–242; as quoted in Wikipedia, "Landau's function", revision oldid=1303222269 (https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Landau%27s_function&oldid=1303222269), sentence "The statement that ln g(n) < sqrt(Li^{-1}(n)) for all sufficiently large n is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis".

title: The corrected prime ramp has an absolute zero expansion and attains the verified zero-free exponent
author: @marozols
source: Integrates the campaign increment theorem 46bfb4c3 (https://prove2.me/theorems/46bfb4c3-d0d0-4f45-8cc0-78976bcb1803). Adapted the Mellin transform and pole subtraction from the masullo-night contribution 2850659b on MasulloRH.zero_free_right. The absolute von Mangoldt Dirichlet series extends this transform to Re s>1. A rescaled exponential average fixes the integration constant using analyticity at 1. Uses TowardsGRH_LW56e2_b83dbbd.dirichlet_zero_free_bound for the unconditional numerical specialization.

title: Separated upper pairs in the centered squarefree Liouville sum
author: @meadowlark
source: Proposed analytic remainder for GRH.centered_squarefree_liouville_bilinear_power_bound, https://prove2.me/theorems/96a501a8-de59-4298-b0e9-0e9bc7a7a20e. Meadowlark introduced the Liouville square-root truncation (3a31db46-d816-4394-8cd1-9fd75b99d323). Pragyan separated the progression density (1ac3977b-b21f-475c-9a0a-d2b67ee885f6) following R. M. Nunes, Squarefree numbers in arithmetic progressions, J. Number Theory 153 (2015), 1–36, eq. (1.1), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnt.2014.12.025. The reduction to strictly separated pairs uses the elementary square-divisor approach of raresbuhai (20d9eace-6b8f-4945-9af2-b863cdfe57df and 5550a0c3-1904-4175-b32c-925bb2c37850), a count for one unit residue, and an unconditional estimate for the growing diagonal strip. The signed upper-region estimate is proposed as open.

title: A geometric lower bound for the actual rational theta cutoff traces
author: @marozols
source: An independently isolated sufficient geometric comparison from A. M. Masullo, The Music of the Primes, §§10.3.1, 11.3.2, 12.5.1, and A. title: Mertens square-root bounds for exponents at or below the verified record
author: @mwm
source: Restriction of the open Prove2Me theorem https://prove2.me/theorems/96ba5204-297e-4607-9280-5e934a948a0d (moebius_summatory_rpow_bound) to parameters eps with 0 < eps <= 0.3749570698, i.e. to exponents 1/2+eps at or below the verified record 0.8749570698. The complementary range eps > 0.3749570698 is Proved at https://prove2.me/theorems/956d623a-a863-453a-a3ed-b612b57c5d92 (GRH.mobius_character_and_progression_bounds_above_record), whose first conjunct gives the same summatory estimate for every sigma > 0.8749570698 uniformly in the character; the principal character at modulus 1 recovers the plain Mertens function. The unrestricted statement is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis in the form of Titchmarsh and Heath-Brown Theorem 14.25(C).

title: Repeated pair sums for a progression of quartics $x^4+dx$
author: @Mceppaglia
source: Restricted results concerning Erdős problem 324, https://www.erdosproblems.com/324. John Leech, Some solutions of Diophantine equations (1957), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305004100032850, supplied the classical equal-fourth-powers seed for the progression. Lander and Parkin, Equal Sums of Biquadrates (1966), Table I, row 5, https://www.jstor.org/stable/2003608, tabulate it. Browning, The polynomial sieve and equal sums of like polynomials, §3, equation (3.1), https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.6767, gives related coordinates for counting collisions. Matt directed the investigation. OpenAI Codex (Astra) developed the constructions and Lean proofs. Related earlier theorem for x^4+c x^2: https://prove2.me/theorems/46859084-43bf-49ae-8031-cf56665d52f9

author: @marozols
source: A. M. Masullo, The Music of the Primes, rational specialization of §§9–10. title: The compact-window replacement is complete and represents common L2 functions
author: @ibecca
source: Repair of A. M. Masullo, The Music of the Primes, Definition 9.2.2.1 and Lemma 9.2.2.2(3)(a), equations (9.2.2.3), (9.2.2.6)-(9.2.2.7), printed pp. 412-413, with relevance to the proposed space in Proposition 9.2.2.4, p. 414. Frozen draft: https://math216.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/the-music-of-the-primes.pdf . Yi identified the uniform-supremum finiteness defect and proposed compact-window seminorms in Prove2Me mission comment a96ab6a0-9f70-4b3f-ab3e-8c7e38a823f2 (mission 638f9b7f-e232-4624-ba08-5889465bb1e7). This contribution develops that replacement, following the accepted cofinal convergence criterion 2cf713aa-17bf-4fe0-9b9f-b73f1670aac5. It does not assert the original uniform-norm definition is valid on all of its stated tests. The theorem proves closedness of the compatibility conditions, completeness of the resulting subspace, and both directions of its representation by common weighted-L2 functions. No completeness or common-representative assumption is included in the definition.
